description:
Parent: op-841p. Condense rung-1 Monte Carlo results into multigroup cross sections the deterministic rung can consume.

ARCHITECTURAL RULE: cross-section code lives in njoy-outram-park-fork; transport crates are data-free and pull from it. So the MGXS generator belongs in the nuclear-data crate and the MC tallies that feed it belong in outram-mc-libs.

DO NOT DUPLICATE the existing work - wire to it:
- op-6tz.15 (in progress): multigroup transport is LIVE. crates/outram-mc-libs/src/physics/physics_mg.rs carries Mgxs, MgxsLibrary and run_keff_mg, verified 2-group infinite medium k_inf 1.10085 +/- 0.00175 vs analytic 1.10000.
- op-6tz.6.3 (in progress): GROUPR elastic scatter matrix and Bondarenko-dilution self-shielding are live on U-235 ENDF/B-VIII.0. Explicitly NOT validated against a real NJOY GENDF golden tape. Open gaps: chi(E'|E) from MF=5, and the URR MF=2/MT=152 tape.

HAND-OFF MUST CARRY: the group structure stated by name; flux-weighted self-shielded cross sections per group per material zone; the scatter matrix with its Legendre order; group chi (prompt, and delayed by precursor group); diffusion coefficients with the definition used (transport-corrected or not) stated; and the statistical uncertainty on every tallied quantity, propagated not dropped.

GROUP STRUCTURE RECOMMENDATION (maintainer decision needed): start with the VTB HTR-10 ten-group structure (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/htr10/steady/htr-10-full.i:196, G = 10), because it is what the only available HTGR reference deck uses. Tantillo et al. note 6 broad groups already give acceptable agreement with Monte Carlo for this reactor type. Whichever is chosen MUST be recorded in the run manifest.

THE FORMAT IS NOT A FILE CONVERSION. See the sibling bead on the nuclearData bridge.
title: HTR-10 rung 2: MGXS generation for the HTR-10 pebble bed, in GeN-Foam nuclearData form

description:
Found 2026-08-13 while porting the fhr_sim_v2 pacer into htgr_sim_v1. op-xvye is filed as affecting 'both simulation loops'; it is actually FOUR sites, and these two are still broken:

  crates/tampines/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/prke_backend/mod.rs:185-194
  crates/tampines/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/mod.rs:1593-1601

Both carry the identical defect pair: an .abs() SIGN COLLAPSE (so running behind schedule is treated the same as
running ahead) and a from_micros(x - 1) UNDERFLOW evaluated BEFORE the guard that would have made it safe.

Left untouched deliberately: this is the maintainer's own code and was outside the reporting agent's scope.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL DUPLICATE: on 2026-08-13 the maintainer directed htgr_sim_v1's pacer to FOLLOW the
fhr_sim_v2 pacer. So the pattern being held up as the house standard is the one carrying the bug. The htgr port used
Duration::saturating_sub and is clean, but anyone copying fhr_sim_v2 next will inherit the defect again.

Fix shape is already proven: the same surgical Duration::saturating_sub replacement applied to the two CIET v2 sites,
preserving branch structure and the 1 ms margin.

See op-xvye for the other two sites and the CIET v2 behaviour change that fix introduced.
title: fhr_sim_v2 carries the op-xvye pacing defect too -- 2 unfixed sites in maintainer's own code

description: GENERAL multiphase (op-v6s.13) needs >1 coupled primary unknown per cell (e.g. gas pressure + saturation + temperature), which the current scalar 1-DOF LduMatrix solver cannot represent. Add a block/interleaved multi-DOF Newton-Krylov layer: block-sparse Jacobian assembly (n_dof_per_cell) over the grid connectivity, block ILU/Jacobi preconditioning, reusing the foam-basic-lib Krylov solvers on the flattened system. Blocks op-v6s.13.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Block multi-DOF Newton-Krylov solver implemented 2026-07-22: BlockLduMatrix (nb-DOF blocks over grid connectivity), BlockJacobiPreconditioner, block_bicgstab, BlockNonlinearSystem trait + BlockNewtonSolver. Verified: block SpMV vs dense 1e-12, block BiCGStab vs dense LU 1e-6, coupled 2-var Newton on manufactured solution. Enables two-phase multiphase (op-v6s.13).

title: Multi-DOF coupled block Newton-Krylov solver (prerequisite for GENERAL multiphase)

description:
Extend crates/kovan-cli/tests/cli_e2e.rs (existing pattern) and add unit tests in kovan-semantics.

MUST PIN:
- Running twice over the same inputs produces BYTE-IDENTICAL output. This is the gate that catches a timestamp, an absolute path, or HashMap iteration order leaking in -- the three ways a 'deterministic' generator stops being one.
- The output directory is flat: assert no subdirectories are created, because the whole point is an upload dialog that cannot take folders.
- A re-run after removing a crate from the selection does not leave the old file behind.
- The token ESTIMATE is reported as an estimate, and the budget check triggers at the right threshold.
- AGENTS.md names the crates that were omitted.

Use tempfile (already a dev-dependency of kovan-cli) with a synthetic crate tree; do not depend on the real crates/ contents, which change.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
PARTIALLY DONE. The determinism gate exists as a kovan-semantics lib test (agent_docs::tests::the_bundle_is_byte_identical_on_a_rerun) with methodology and results in its doc comment: two runs into separate directories, every file compared byte-for-byte, plus assertions that the output is flat and that a deselected crate's file does not survive a regeneration. 42 lib tests pass.

STILL OPEN: nothing has been added to crates/kovan-cli/tests/cli_e2e.rs, so the CLI surface itself -- argument parsing, --list, --budget, the core-vs-optional report -- is untested end to end.

title: agent-docs: e2e test + determinism gate
